slice 5.7: BDEV band + `memory` ramdisk driver + `tools/mkfs-mfs` + rootfs blob

Builds the bottom two layers of the storage stack Phase 5's milestone needs
(D3): a MinixFS v3 image built at compile time, packed into the MXBI archive as
a non-ELF blob, copied into RAM frames and mapped into the `memory` driver's
address space at boot, and served over a new BDEV request band. Slice 5.8 puts
MFS on top of it; 5.9 closes the milestone.

ABI. `BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00`, between VFS (`0x800`) and CDEV (`0xB00`), leaving
`0x900` for 5.8's VFS<->FS band — four in-tree comments recorded that pairing
the other way round and are corrected here; only ascending order is
load-bearing. Payload mirrors CDEV: `{minor, grant, len, block}`, with **no
granter field** (the driver takes it from the kernel-stamped `m_source`, the
5.2/5.3 confused-deputy rule) and **no grant-offset field** (every client
through 5.9 grants a buffer whose block starts at 0). Reply `m_type` is the
byte count.

Two deliberate departures from CDEV. An over-long or out-of-range request is
`EINVAL`, not a short read: a short *write* is a POSIX contract clients loop
over, but a filesystem cannot interpret half a block, and `EIO` stays reserved
for Phase 6's real media errors. And `BDEV_WRITE` is defined now and answers
`EROFS`, not `ENOSYS` — `ENOSYS` is already the unknown-`m_type` answer, so
reusing it would make "doesn't know about writes" and "knows and refuses"
indistinguishable. It validates before refusing, so 5.10 replaces one line.

Kernel. `uspace::RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE = 0x8000_0000` (one L1 slot, 4 MiB) sits
*above* the device window on purpose: `region::REGION_LIMIT` is the base of the
lowest kernel-owned window, so VM needs no edit when a window is added. The
pre-map is a `nr == MEM_PROC_NR` arm in `load_boot_server` beside TTY's — not in
`load_exec_image`, which `do_exec` shares — with no TLB or cache maintenance
(both justified in situ) and no `prot.device` involvement, since these are
ordinary RAM frames. Every step `.expect()`s: a non-advancing loop must panic on
`AlreadyMapped`, not leave a 1-page ramdisk and 255 leaked frames. New

## What the section says

- **The trailer is the DCO attestation, not a style choice** — it asserts the right to contribute under BSD-3-Clause. `--signoff` signs off *as the committer*, so hand-writing one for another author defeats the purpose.
- **Sign-off is orthogonal to GPG signing.** `--signoff` is the DCO trailer, `--gpg-sign` (on by default here) is the cryptographic signature. Both are required and neither substitutes for the other; the global never-`--no-gpg-sign` / never-`--no-verify` rules still hold.
- **Presence is the invariant, not trailer order** — see below.
- **GitHub UI merge commits have no sign-off**, which is expected and not worth fixing. Only the authored commits inside a PR need one.

## The ordering claim corrected itself mid-PR

The first draft prescribed a fixed footer order — `Co-Authored-By:` → `Entire-Checkpoint:` → `Signed-off-by:` — which is exactly what the last six commits look like:

```
9dcb3cf: Co-Authored-By Entire-Checkpoint Signed-off-by
5aa9d35: Co-Authored-By Entire-Checkpoint Signed-off-by

```

Then this commit came out `Co-Authored-By` → `Signed-off-by` → `Entire-Checkpoint`, because the hook inserting the checkpoint trailer can run either side of the commit. Both orderings are already in the history and neither is wrong, so the guidance now states the invariant that actually holds — the sign-off is *present* — with the verification command:

```sh
git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Signed-off-by)'
```

Worth flagging because a doc contradicted by the commit that introduces it is worse than no doc.

## Enforcement

Convention only. There is no DCO gate in `ci.yml`, so this is enforced by reading `CLAUDE.md`, not by a red check. Happy to add one (GitHub's DCO app, or a `git log` job alongside the existing ten gates) as a follow-up if you want it mechanical.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# tools/check-dco.sh -- verify every non-merge commit in a range carries a
# Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off matching its author.
#
#   usage: tools/check-dco.sh [<range>]
#
# Default range is <merge-base with the default branch>..HEAD, i.e. the commits
# this branch adds. CI passes an explicit <base-sha>..<head-sha> for the PR.
#
# A commit passes when it carries a `Signed-off-by:` trailer whose email
# matches the commit author's, case-insensitively. Matching on *email* and not
# the display name is deliberate: the email is the identity the DCO attests to,
# while names get typo'd, transliterated, and reformatted by tooling.
#
# Merge commits are skipped -- GitHub's UI writes them and cannot sign them
# off, which is expected and documented in CLAUDE.md's "Commits" section.
#
# An empty range is a FAILURE, not a vacuous pass: the only caller is a PR gate
# where zero authored commits means the range was computed wrong, and a gate
# that goes green on a broken range is worse than no gate. Every violation is
# reported (not just the first) before the non-zero exit, so one run shows the
# whole story.

set -euo pipefail

if [[ $# -gt 1 ]]; then
    echo "usage: $0 [<range>]" >&2
    exit 64
fi

if [[ $# -eq 1 ]]; then
    RANGE="$1"
else
    # Prefer the remote-tracking tip so the range is right on a branch whose
    # local `main` is stale; fall back to a local `main` for offline use.
    for base in origin/main main; do
        if git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null; then
            RANGE="$(git merge-base "$base" HEAD)..HEAD"
            break
        fi
    done
    if [[ -z "${RANGE:-}" ]]; then
        echo "error: no origin/main or main to diff against; pass a range" >&2
        exit 64
    fi
fi

if ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${RANGE%%..*}" >/dev/null; then
    echo "error: bad range (left side unknown): $RANGE" >&2
    exit 66
fi

# --no-merges: see the header. Read into an array so the loop body runs in this
# shell and its `fail` assignments survive (a pipe would subshell them away).
mapfile -t commits < <(git rev-list --no-merges "$RANGE")

if [[ "${#commits[@]}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "FAIL: no non-merge commits in range $RANGE"
    echo "    A PR always adds at least one authored commit, so this almost"
    echo "    certainly means the range is wrong rather than that the branch"
    echo "    is clean. Check the base/head SHAs before trusting this gate."
    exit 1
fi

fail=0

for sha in "${commits[@]}"; do
    author="$(git log -1 --format='%ae' "$sha")"
    subject="$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$sha")"
    # One trailer per line; a commit may legitimately carry several (e.g. a
    # patch relayed by a maintainer), and any one matching the author is enough.
    signoffs="$(git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Signed-off-by,valueonly)' "$sha")"

    matched=0
    while IFS= read -r trailer; do
        [[ -z "$trailer" ]] && continue
        # `Name <email>` -> `email`; a trailer with no angle brackets is
        # malformed and simply will not match.
        email="${trailer##*<}"
        email="${email%%>*}"
        if [[ "${email,,}" == "${author,,}" ]]; then
            matched=1
            break
        fi
    done <<< "$signoffs"

    if [[ "$matched" -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "NO SIGN-OFF  ${sha:0:12}  $subject"
        echo "    author:   $author"
        if [[ -z "$signoffs" ]]; then
            echo "    trailers: (none) -- recommit with: git commit --amend --signoff"
        else
            echo "    trailers: $(echo "$signoffs" | tr '\n' ';')"
            echo "    none of those match the author; --signoff signs off as"
            echo "    the committer, so the author must add their own."
        fi
        fail=1
    fi
done

if [[ "$fail" -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo "FAIL: $RANGE has commits without a DCO sign-off (see above)"
    echo "    Fix the most recent one with:  git commit --amend --signoff"
    echo "    Fix a whole branch with:       git rebase --signoff <base>"
    exit 1
fi
echo "PASS: all ${#commits[@]} non-merge commits in $RANGE are signed off"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# tools/check-dco.sh -- verify every non-merge commit in a range carries a
# Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off matching its author.
#
#   usage: tools/check-dco.sh [<range>]
#
# Default range is <merge-base with the default branch>..HEAD, i.e. the commits
# this branch adds. CI passes an explicit <base-sha>..<head-sha> for the PR.
#

# matches the commit author's, case-insensitively. Matching on *email* and not

# while names get typo'd, transliterated, and reformatted by tooling.

# Merge commits are skipped -- GitHub's UI writes them and cannot sign them
# off, which is expected and documented in CLAUDE.md's "Commits" section.
#

# where zero authored commits means the range was computed wrong, and a gate
# that goes green on a broken range is worse than no gate. Every violation is
# reported (not just the first) before the non-zero exit, so one run shows the
# whole story.
#
# Kept to bash 3.2 (no `mapfile`, no `${var,,}`) so it runs on a stock macOS
# /bin/bash as well as CI's bash 5 -- a check you cannot run before pushing is
# a check you find out about from a red X.

set -euo pipefail

if [[ $# -gt 1 ]]; then
    echo "usage: $0 [<range>]" >&2
    exit 64
fi

RANGE=""
if [[ $# -eq 1 ]]; then
    RANGE="$1"
else
    # Prefer the remote-tracking tip so the range is right on a branch whose
    # local `main` is stale; fall back to a local `main` for offline use.
    for base in origin/main main; do
        if git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null; then
            RANGE="$(git merge-base "$base" HEAD)..HEAD"
            break
        fi
    done
    if [[ -z "$RANGE" ]]; then
        echo "error: no origin/main or main to diff against; pass a range" >&2
        exit 64
    fi
fi

if ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${RANGE%%..*}" >/dev/null; then
    echo "error: bad range (left side unknown): $RANGE" >&2
    exit 66
fi

lower() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; }

# Hex SHAs are safe to word-split on, which keeps this bash 3.2 clean (no
# `mapfile`) and keeps the loop body in this shell, where `fail` survives.
commits="$(git rev-list --no-merges "$RANGE")"

if [[ -z "$commits" ]]; then
    echo "FAIL: no non-merge commits in range $RANGE"
    echo "    A PR always adds at least one authored commit, so this almost"
    echo "    certainly means the range is wrong rather than that the branch"
    echo "    is clean. Check the base/head SHAs before trusting this gate."
    exit 1
fi

fail=0
checked=0

for sha in $commits; do
    checked=$((checked + 1))
    author="$(git log -1 --format='%ae' "$sha")"
    subject="$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$sha")"
    # One trailer per line; a commit may legitimately carry several (e.g. a
    # patch relayed by a maintainer), and any one matching the author suffices.
    signoffs="$(git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Signed-off-by,valueonly)' "$sha")"

    matched=0
    while IFS= read -r trailer; do
        [[ -z "$trailer" ]] && continue
        # `Name <email>` -> `email`; a trailer with no angle brackets is
        # malformed and simply will not match.
        email="${trailer##*<}"
        email="${email%%>*}"
        if [[ "$(lower "$email")" == "$(lower "$author")" ]]; then
            matched=1
            break
        fi
    done <<< "$signoffs"

    if [[ "$matched" -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "NO SIGN-OFF  ${sha:0:12}  $subject"
        echo "    author:   $author"
        if [[ -z "$signoffs" ]]; then
            echo "    trailers: (none) -- recommit with: git commit --amend --signoff"
        else
            echo "    trailers: $(echo "$signoffs" | tr '\n' ';')"
            echo "    none of those match the author; --signoff signs off as"
            echo "    the committer, so the author must add their own."
        fi
        fail=1
    fi
done

if [[ "$fail" -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo "FAIL: $RANGE has commits without a DCO sign-off (see above)"
    echo "    Fix the most recent one with:  git commit --amend --signoff"
    echo "    Fix a whole branch with:       git rebase --signoff <base>"

ci: blocking DCO sign-off gate (tools/check-dco.sh)

Makes the sign-off rule the previous commit documents enforceable, so it
is caught by a red X rather than by someone remembering to read
CLAUDE.md. Eleven gates now; `dco` blocks.

The check is a script, not inline YAML, following the
tools/check-boot-log.sh precedent: the whole point of a pre-push rule is
being able to run it before pushing. Bare `tools/check-dco.sh` defaults
to `<merge-base with origin/main>..HEAD`; CI passes the PR's explicit
base..head. Kept to bash 3.2 (no `mapfile`, no `${var,,}`) so it runs on
a stock macOS /bin/bash and not only on CI's bash 5 — a check that only
works on the runner is a check you learn about too late.

Three decisions worth recording:

- It matches the sign-off's *email* against the commit author's,
  case-insensitively, not the display name. The email is the identity
  the DCO attests to, while names get typo'd and reformatted by tooling.
  This is what catches a trailer naming someone else — a relayed patch
  needs its author's own sign-off.
- An empty range is a FAILURE. Zero authored commits means the range was
  computed wrong, and a gate that goes green on a broken range is worse
  than no gate. Same reasoning the boot-marker work keeps running into:
  encode the pass, never the absence of a failure.
- PR-only (`if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`). A push to main
  lands a GitHub merge commit that by design carries no sign-off, and
  the authored commits beneath it were already checked on their own PR.
  It needs `fetch-depth: 0` — the default shallow clone has neither
  endpoint — and passes the SHAs via `env:` rather than interpolating
  `${{ }}` into `run:`, the standard expression-injection guard, kept
  even though these two fields are hex.

Verified against real and synthetic history: PASS over all 102 non-merge
commits in the repo; FAIL (exit 1, both offenders reported, not just the
first) for a missing trailer and for one naming a different author; FAIL
on an empty range; merge commits skipped and an UPPERCASE-email trailer
matched, both confirmed absent from a failing report. shellcheck clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
